akhfash:5-5.t: He said ﴿فَجَعَلَهُمْ كَعَصْفٍ مَّأْكُولِ﴾. «[Translator's note: the source gives no comment after the quotation.]»

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ﴾: an interrogative of wonder (istifhām taʿajjub), that is, wonder at ﴿كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأَصْحَابِ الْفِيلِ﴾. It [the elephant] was Maḥmūd, and its companions were Abraha, king of Yemen, and his army. He built a church in Ṣanʿāʾ in order to divert the pilgrims to it from Mecca. A man of Kināna relieved himself in it and smeared its qibla with excrement in contempt of it. So Abraha swore that he would surely demolish the Kaʿba, and he came to Mecca with his army on elephants, at their head Maḥmūd. When they set out to demolish the Kaʿba, Allah sent upon them what He related in His words:

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿أَلَمْ يَجْعَلْ﴾, that is, He made ﴿كَيْدَهُمْ﴾ in demolishing the Kaʿba ﴿فِي تَضْلِيلٍ﴾: loss and destruction,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَأَرْسَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ طَيْرًا أَبَابِيلَ﴾: flock upon flock. It is said that it has no singular, like «أساطير»; and it is said its singular is «إبّول» or «إبّال» or «إبّيل», like «عجّول», «مفتاح» and «سكّين»,

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿فَجَعَلَهُمْ كَعَصْفٍ مَأْكُولٍ﴾: like the leaves of crops that animals have eaten, trampled and destroyed; that is, Allah the Exalted destroyed every one of them with his own stone on which his name was written. It was larger than a lentil and smaller than a chickpea; it pierced the helmet, the man and the elephant and reached the ground. This was in the year of the birth of the Prophet ﷺ.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ﴾ the hamza is a particle of affirmative interrogation (istifhām taqrīrī), and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, the sign of its jussive being the omission of the weak letter from its end, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿كَيْفَ﴾ an interrogative noun, mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause stands in place of the two objects of ترى. ﴿بِأَصْحابِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْفِيلِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿أَلَمْ يَجْعَلْ﴾ the hamza is a particle of affirmative interrogation (istifhām taqrīrī), and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿كَيْدَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فِي تَضْلِيلٍ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَأَرْسَلَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿طَيْراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿أَبابِيلَ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿تَرْمِيهِمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿بِحِجارَةٍ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مِنْ سِجِّيلٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of حجارة; the clause is a second adjective of طيرا.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿فَجَعَلَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its object, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿كَعَصْفٍ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the two are in the position of the second object. ﴿مَأْكُولٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of عصف; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it.

dervis-irab:1-5.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْفِيلِ): one of the largest of animals; it has a long trunk with which it raises fodder and water to its mouth and with which it strikes. Its plurals are afyāl, fiyala and fuyūl, and its feminine is fīla. Al-fīl is also the base, heavy [dull] person. Dāʾ al-fīl (elephantiasis) is a disease from which a dense thickening arises in the foot and the leg, interspersed with small protruding knots. Al-fayyāl is the keeper of the elephant, plural fayyāla. Fāl al-raʾy, fāʾiluhu and fayyiluhu: weak in judgement; and al-fiyāla is weakness of judgement.
(تَضْلِيلٍ): loss, ruin and destruction. Imruʾ al-Qays was called «the errant king» (al-malik al-ḍillīl) because he lost (ḍallala) his father's kingdom, i.e. let it be lost.
(طَيْراً): al-ṭayr is a generic noun, treated as masculine and as feminine. Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim recited, on the masculine use of al-ṭayr:
لقد تركت فؤادك مستهاما ... مطوّقة على فنن تغنّى
تميل به وتركبه بلحن ... إذا ما عنّ للمحزون أنا
فلا يغررك أيام تولّى ... بذكراها ولا طير أرنّا
(A ring-dove singing on a branch has left your heart distraught; she sways on it and mounts it with a melody, whenever a moan occurs to the grief-stricken. So let not days that have passed deceive you with their memory, nor a bird that has cried out.)
(أَبابِيلَ): Ibn Khālawayh said: «"أبابيل" is an adjective of "الطير", i.e. flocks; its singular is ibbawl, like ʿijjawl and ʿajājīl. Abū Jaʿfar al-Ruʾāsī said: its singular is ibbīl. Others said: abābīl has no singular, and similar to it are asāṭīr, and "the people went off in shamāṭīṭ, ʿabābīd and ʿabādīd" — of all of these no singular has been heard. Others said: the singular of asāṭīr is usṭūra. Al-abīl, in a sense other than this, is the monk, and al-wabīl is the staff. One says: I saw an abīl, i.e. a monk, leaning on a wabīl, driving an afīl. Al-afīl is the young of the she-camel. ʿAdī said:
أبلغ النعمان عنّي مالكا ... قول من خاف اظّنانا واعتذر
إنني والله، فاقبل حلفتي ... بأبيل كلما صلّى جأر»
(Convey to al-Nuʿmān from me a message, the word of one who feared suspicion and offered excuse: I, by Allah — so accept my oath — and by a monk who cries aloud whenever he prays ...)
Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: «Abābīl: flocks (kharāʾiq); the singular is ibbāla. Among their proverbs: "ضغث على إبالة" (a handful [of grass] on top of a bundle) — it is the large bundle; the flock of birds, in its packing together, was likened to the bundle. It is also said that abābīl is like ʿabābīd and shamāṭīṭ, having no singular.» In al-Qāmūs: «Abābīl: troops, a plural without a singular. Al-ibāla — like ijjāna, and it may be lightened, and like sikkīt, ʿijjawl and dīnār — is a group of birds, horses or camels, or those of them following one another.»
(سِجِّيلٍ): baked, burnt clay, like brick. Al-Zamakhsharī's wording:
«Sijjīl is as though it were a proper name for the register in which the punishment of the unbelievers was written, just as sijjīn is a proper name for the register of their deeds; as if it were said: with stones from among the punishment that is written and recorded. Its derivation is from al-isjāl, which is sending forth, because punishment is described as such: "وأرسل عليهم طيرا", "فأرسلنا عليهم الطوفان". From Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both: of clay baked as brick is baked. It is also said it is arabicised from sang-o-gil [Persian, "stone and clay"], and it is said: from what is severe of His punishment. They related the verse of Ibn Muqbil "ضربا تواصت به الأبطال سجيلا", whereas it is in fact "سجينا", and the ode rhymes in nūn and is well known in his dīwān.» I say: it is a fine ode, and at its beginning comes:
طاف الخيال بنا ركبا يمانينا ... ودون ليلى عواد لو تعدينا
وإن فينا صبوحا إن رأيت به ... ركبا مهيبا وآلاما هما فينا
ورفقة يضربون البيض ضاحية ... ضربا تواصت به الأبطال سجينا
(The phantom visited us, riders of Yemen, while before Laylā lie obstacles, could you but cross them; and among us is a morning draught — if you would see it — a fearsome band of riders and coats of mail, both among us; and companions who strike the helmets in broad day, with a blow the heroes enjoined upon one another, a fettering blow.)
By the phantom he meant the apparition of his beloved Laylā. «ركبا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «بنا». «يمانين» is the plural of yamān, whose origin is yamānī; the yāʾ was abandoned because the alif remains, indicating the relation (nisba). The circumstance is that between us and Laylā there is a long distance and obstacles that hinder. Then he turned to her [in address] and said: if you were to cross them, you would find them many, preventing you from visiting [us]. The circumstance is that among us are horsemen clad in their arms. He borrowed for them [the word] «صبوح», which is a name for wine at morning time, the common factor being that each of them comes in the morning; and there is in it mockery of his enemies. «ركبا» [follows], and «إن رأيت», i.e. if you wish to know of it, is a parenthesis whose apodosis is omitted because the speech indicates it. «المهيب» is a passive participle: the one whom people hold in awe and fear. «ألام» is the plural of laʾm, like shajar, its singular being laʾma, like shajara; it is a small coat of mail worn in war, and what is meant is either the thing itself or the horsemen wearing it. «هما», i.e. the coats of mail and the riders, are among us. «رفقة» is conjoined to «ركبا». «البيض» is an allusion to swords; «ضاحية» means openly, i.e. they strike with them. It may also be read with fatḥa on the bāʾ (al-bayḍ), i.e. the helmets worn on the heads, meaning by them the heads themselves. «السجين» is the severe [blow] that stops the movement of the slain, as if from al-sijn, which is imprisonment. This is the transmission from Ibn Muqbil; some related it as «سجيلا» with lām, i.e. severe, as if from al-tasjīl, i.e. strengthening and making firm; but the ode rhymes in nūn, as you have seen. Al-Bukhārī said in his Ṣaḥīḥ: «sijjīn and sijjīl — lām and nūn are sisters», and then he related the verse.
As for Ibn Khālawayh, he claimed that al-sijjīl is the severe. He said: «It is also said: stone and clay; the origin is sang and gil, and it was arabicised.»
(عصف): al-ʿaṣf — its explanation has preceded; it is the leaves of crops and the fine particles of straw.

* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأَصْحابِ الْفِيلِ): the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī); «لم» is a particle of negation, of conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning], and of the jussive; «تر» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by «لم», the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter. In what follows is the text of Ibn Khālawayh's wording, for it fully serves the purpose: «The pattern of "تر" in terms of the verb [-template] is taf [i.e. reduced from tafʿal]; two letters have been dropped from its end: the alif and the hamza. The alif fell because of the jussive; it is the lām (third radical) of the verb, changed from yāʾ. The hamza is the ʿayn (second radical) of the verb; it fell for lightening. The origin is "ترأى" [taraʾā]: the yāʾ was changed to alif because it was vowelled and the letter before it had fatḥa, so it became alif in pronunciation and yāʾ in writing. They transferred the fatḥa of the hamza to the rāʾ and dropped [the hamza] for lightening, because the past of "ترى" is "رأيت", with hamza, and the maṣdar of that: raʾaytu Zaydan bi-ʿaynī, arāhu, ruʾyatan, so I am rāʾin. The pattern of rāʾin is fāʿil, its origin being rāʾiyun: they found the ḍamma heavy on the final yāʾ and dropped it, so two quiescent letters met, the yāʾ and the tanwīn, and they dropped the yāʾ because of the meeting of the two quiescent letters, so it became rāʾin, like rāʿin and qāḍin. The hamza in rāʾin corresponds to the ʿayn in rāʿin. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «بإزالة» (by removal), evidently for «بإزاء» (corresponding to).] If you wish, you write it out, putting a yāʾ after the alif in place of the hamza; and if you wish, you write it with alif and do not write the hamza, because when the hamza comes after alif it is concealed in pause, so they dropped it in writing. Likewise jāʾin, shāʾin, sāʾin, and marāʾin, the plural of mirʾāt: in all of that you have the choice between dropping and writing it. When you form the imperative of raʾaytu, you say "رَ يا زيد" (see, O Zayd!) with a single rāʾ, and when you pause you say "رَهْ". The imperative came to be a single letter, while the origin is three, only because the hamza fell for lightening and the alif fell for the jussive, so the imperative remained on one letter. Similar, among [verbs] whose two ends are weak so that the imperative remains on one letter, is the saying of the Arabs: "عِ كلامي" (heed my words), "شِ ثوبك" (embroider your garment), "قِ زيدا" (protect Zayd), "لِ الأمر" (take charge of the matter), "فِ بالوعد" (fulfil the promise). Their origin is from wafā yafī, waʿā yaʿī, washā yashī and waliya yalī: the yāʾ went for the jussive, and the wāw because it fell between a yāʾ and a kasra, so the imperative remained on one letter. Allah the Exalted said: "وقنا عذاب النار"; the origin is "اوقينا" — the yāʾ went for the jussive and the wāw because it fell between two kasras, so a single qāf remained. So you say: "قِ يا زيد", "قِيا", "قُوا". Allah the Exalted said: "يا أيها الذين آمنوا قوا أنفسكم". Likewise you say: "رَ يا زيد", "رَيا" for two, "رَوا" for a group, "رَيْ يا هند", "رَيا" like the masculine [dual], and "رَيْن يا نسوة". When you pause on all of that, you say "عِهْ" and "قِهْ", with the hāʾ and nothing else.»
«كيف» is an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative, as a maṣdar [i.e. absolute object] or as a ḥāl. Ibn Hishām chose the first in al-Mughnī; he said: «In my view it also comes in this type as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and of this is "كيف فعل ربك", since the meaning is "what doing did your Lord do"; it is not plausible here that it be a ḥāl of the agent» — i.e. «ربك» — because that would require that the agent, the Lord, be qualified by modes and states, since the meaning [would be]: your Lord acted, in the state of being in what condition and mode — and His being qualified by them is impossible. The clause suspended [from the verb] by the interrogative stands in place of the two objects of «تر», because the seeing is mental, conveying necessary knowledge equal in strength and clarity to witnessing and eyesight. «بأصحاب الفيل» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «فعل».
(أَلَمْ يَجْعَلْ كَيْدَهُمْ فِي تَضْلِيلٍ): the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation; «لم» is a particle of negation, conversion and the jussive; «يجعل» is an imperfect verb, jussive by «لم»; the agent is latent, its implied form being «هو», referring to Allah the Exalted; «كيدهم» is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and «في تضليل» is in the position of the second object.
(وَأَرْسَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ طَيْراً أَبابِيلَ): the wāw is a conjunction, and «أرسل» is conjoined to «ألم نجعل» [Translator's note: so in the text; the verse reads «ألم يجعل»], because the interrogative in it is for affirmation, so the meaning was: He did make that. Its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; «عليهم» is attached to «أرسل»; «طيرا» is a direct object; and «أبابيل» is a naʿt (adjective) of «طيرا», because it is a collective noun.
(تَرْمِيهِمْ بِحِجارَةٍ مِنْ سِجِّيلٍ): the clause is a second adjective of «طيرا». «ترميهم» is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object; «بحجارة» is attached to «ترميهم»; and «من سجيل» is an adjective of «حجارة».
(فَجَعَلَهُمْ كَعَصْفٍ مَأْكُولٍ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; «جعلهم» is a past verb and a latent agent; the hāʾ is the first direct object; «كعصف» is in the position of the second object; and «مأكول» is an adjective of «عصف».

* Benefits:
The story of the People of the Elephant is one of the outstanding Arab stories. It is a lengthy one; the exegetes and the biographers of the Prophet have mentioned it at length and in brief. Its gist is that the Negus, king of Abyssinia — Aṣḥama, grandfather of the Negus who believed in the Prophet ﷺ — had sent Abraha as governor over Yemen. He settled there and his authority became firm there, and he built a church to divert the pilgrims to it from Mecca. A man of Kināna defiled it, so Abraha swore that he would surely demolish the Kaʿba. He came to Mecca with his army on elephants, and when they set out to demolish the Kaʿba, Allah sent against them what He has related. Refer to the lengthy works. That was in the year of the birth of the Prophet ﷺ.

farraa:1-1.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأَصْحَابِ ٱلْفِيلِ﴾.
He says: have you not been told about the Abyssinians? They had marched against the House and the people of Mecca. When they were at Dhū al-Majāz, they passed by a herdsman of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and drove off his camels. He mounted his riding animal and came to Mecca, cried out the cry of alarm, and then told them the news. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib leapt onto the back of his horse and caught up with them. Two men of Kinda and Ḥaḍramawt said to him: Go back [149/a] — they were friends of his. He said: By Allah, I will not leave until I take my camels or am taken with them. So they said to Aṣḥama, the chief of the Abyssinians: Give them back to him, for he will take them [back] in the morning [anyway]. So he returned with his camels and told the people of Mecca the news. They stayed for some days seeing nothing; then ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib went back to their place, and behold, they were as Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: "كالْعَصْف المَأْكُولِ" (like devoured straw). Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, had sent against them birds carrying in their beaks stones like sheep droppings; the bird would let go of the stone and it would not miss its man's head, and it would come out of his backside; so they killed them all. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib took of the yellow and the white — meaning gold and silver — as much as he wished, then returned to the people of Mecca and told them; and they went out to their camp and [plundered] what was in it. [Translator's note: the source has «فانتبهوا» (they became aware of), apparently for «فانتهبوا» (they plundered); translated by the latter.]

farraa:3-3.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَبَابِيلَ﴾.
It has no singular, like الشماطيط, العباديد and الشعارير [Translator's note: all words for scattered groups]; for none of these is a singular used. Al-Ruʾāsī — and he was trustworthy and reliable — claimed to me that he had heard its singular: إِبَّالة, with no yāʾ in it. And I have heard among the Arabs one who says: "ضِغث على إبَّالة" (a handful [of grass] on top of a bundle), meaning: plenty on top of plenty. As for «الإيبالة», it is the surplus of fodder that is on top of the load of a donkey or camel; it is like "plenty on plenty", and a load on top of a load. So if someone said: the singular of «الأبابيل» is إيبالة, it would be correct, as they said: دينار, دنانير. And one of the grammarians — al-Kisāʾī — said: I used to hear the grammarians say: أبوك, like العِجّول and العجاجيل. [Translator's note: «أبوك» is as printed; the parallel with «عجّول / عجاجيل» indicates the singular «إبّول».]

farraa:4-4.t: And it is said: ﴿سِجِّيلٍ﴾ is like baked brick, cooked from clay. Al-Kalbī said: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to me; he said: I saw in the house of Umm Hāniʾ bint Abī Ṭālib about a qafīz [Translator's note: a dry measure] of those stones, black and streaked with red.

farraa:5-5.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَعَصْفٍ﴾.
«العصف» is the tips of the crop before it ripens and forms ears.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «كيف»: an interrogative noun, mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), the meaning being: what deed did your Lord do? The clause «فعل» stands in place of the two objects of «تر», which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: (ألم يجعل كيدهم في تضليل) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The preposition «في تضليل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) second object.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The clause «ترميهم» is a second naʿt (adjective) of {طَيْرًا}.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «فجعلهم» is conjoined to the clause «أرسل»; the preposition «كَعَصْفٍ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He (كيف فعل ربك): (كيف) is an adverb, and the governing word (ʿāmil) in it is (فعل). (تر) does not govern it, because it contains the meaning of interrogation, and what precedes it does not govern it. Because of its resemblance to the alif [Translator's note: i.e. the interrogative hamza] it is indeclinable (mabnī), and it is built on the fatḥa because of the quiescence of what precedes it, and because the kasra after the yāʾ is heavy. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «ولأنه ياء الكسر بعد الياء ثقيله», which is garbled; it has been rendered according to its evident sense.]

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying (أبابيل): its singular is «إبّول», like «عجّول» and «عجاجيل»; and it was said: its singular is «إبّيل», like «سكّين» and «سكاكين»; and it was said: its singular is «إبّال», like «دينار» and «دنانير» — the origin of «دينار» being «دنّار», the proof of which is the repetition of the nūn in the plural and the diminutive. And it was said: it is a plural that has no singular; and it was said: it is a collective noun (ism li-l-jamʿ).

mekki-muskil:4-4.t: His saying (ترميهم): in the position of the accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of (طير); likewise (أبابيل) is a naʿt of (طير), as though He said: scattered groups.

mekki-muskil:5-5.t: His saying (كعصف): the kāf is in the position of the accusative, the second object of (جعل), because it has the meaning of «صيّر» (made into).

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿ألم﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīrī), and «لم» is a particle of negation, conversion (to the past) and jussive.
﴿تر﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the agent is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you" (أنت); the clause ﴿ألم تر﴾ is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.
﴿كيف﴾: an interrogative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the place of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿أصحاب الفيل﴾; or in the position of accusative standing in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), the meaning being: "what manner of dealing did your Lord deal?" (أيّ فعل فعل ربك؟)
﴿فعل﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa.
﴿ربك﴾: «رب» is fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, and it is muḍāf, and the kāf is the pronoun of the addressee, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿بأصحاب﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition, and «أصحاب» is a noun genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ, the sign of its genitive being the kasra, and it is muḍāf; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿فعل﴾.
﴿الفيل﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive by the kasra; the clause ﴿كيف فعل ربك﴾ stands in place of the two objects of ﴿ترَ﴾, because the seeing is of the heart (qalbiyya).

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿ألم﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīrī), and «لم» is a particle of negation, conversion (to the past) and jussive.
﴿يجعل﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, the sign of its jussive being the sukūn, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "He" (هو), referring back to Allah the Exalted.
﴿كيدهم﴾: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿يجعل﴾, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa; the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and the mīm is the sign of the plural.
﴿في تضليل﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second object of ﴿يجعل﴾; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿وأرسل﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «أرسل» is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "He" (هو).
﴿عليهم﴾: «على» is a preposition, the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the kasra in the position of genitive, and the mīm is the sign of the plural; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أرسل﴾.
﴿طيرا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿أبابيل﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿طيرا﴾, accusative by the fatḥa; the clause ﴿أرسل...﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿ألم يجعل...﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿ترميهم﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by a ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ because of heaviness, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "they" (هي), referring back to the birds, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on the kasra in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿بحجارة﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ترميهم﴾.
﴿من سجيل﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «حجارة»; the clause ﴿ترميهم﴾ is in the position of accusative as a second naʿt of ﴿طيرا﴾.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿فجعلهم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «جعلهم» is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "He" (هو); the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of accusative as first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the mīm is the sign of the plural.
﴿كعصف﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (مثل), indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative as second mafʿūl bihi, and ﴿عصف﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿مأكول﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿عصف﴾, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra; the clause ﴿جعلهم﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿أرسل﴾, with no grammatical position.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: The alif was dropped from ترى for the jussive. The original has a hamza (ترأى); the vowel of the hamza was cast onto the rāʾ and the hamza was dropped. «كيف» is in the position of the accusative by فعل; it is not declined because it is in the sense of particles, even though it is a noun, and the fāʾ took fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: I.e., in frustration of what they intended.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
Among the best things narrated about it from the early (scholars) is what ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad, who said: ʿAffān narrated to us, saying: Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh: طَيْراً أَبابِيلَ, he said: (in) groups. And it was read before Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar, from Yūsuf ibn Mūsā, who said: Shihāb narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from Ḥumayd, from Abū Khālid, from Abū Ṣāliḥ: «طيرا أبابيل», he said: gathering after gathering.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is well known in the speech of the Arabs: "they came abābīl", i.e., group after group, a great, numerous group after a group. It is derived from abala ʿalayhi, when it became numerous and gathered; and from this the camels (ibil) were named, because of the greatness of their build. It has been said that the meaning of أَفَلا يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَى الْإِبِلِ كَيْفَ خُلِقَتْ [al-Ghāshiya: 17] is that they are the clouds, because of their greatness, even though al-Qutabī rejected this interpretation without an established proof. The most correct thing said about the singular of al-abābīl is what Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: its singular is ibbīl, like sikkīn and sakākīn.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: The kāf is in the position of the accusative as a second object, i.e., (like straw) whose contents have been eaten — it is the husk of the wheat. It may also be in the sense of "eaten by livestock".

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(the hamza) is for confirmatory interrogation [Note: or for expressing wonder.], (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative, a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, i.e. "He did a mighty deed" [Note: or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl whose governing element is a verb.], (بأصحاب) is attached to (فعل)..
Clause: «لم تر ... » has no grammatical position; it is inceptive.
And the clause: «فعل ربّك ... » is in the position of accusative, standing in for the two objects of تر, which is suspended by the interrogative كيف.

* Morphology:
(الفيل): the name of the well-known animal; its wazn is فعل with kasra then sukūn.

* Benefits:
- The Companions of the Elephant:
Historians and biographers mention that Abraha ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ, king of Yemen, built a church in Ṣanʿāʾ and called it al-Qullays, and wished to divert the pilgrims to it. A man from Kināna went out and sat in it at night and defiled it, which angered him. It was also said: a party of Arabs lit a fire, the wind carried it and it burned the church. So he swore to demolish the Kaʿba. He set out with the Abyssinians, and with him an elephant named Maḥmūd, which was strong and huge, and twelve other elephants. When the army came, ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib went out to him and offered him a third of the wealth of Tihāma if he would turn back, but he refused and headed to demolish the Kaʿba. Whenever they directed the elephant toward the Sanctuary it knelt and would not budge, and if they directed it toward Yemen or Syria it trotted. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent birds, each bird carrying a stone in its beak and two stones in its feet, smaller than a chickpea. The stone would fall on a man's head and come out of his rear; so they fled and perished. Abraha died, his chest splitting open from his heart. His vizier escaped, with a bird hovering over him, until he reached the Negus and told him the story; when he finished it, the stone fell on him and he dropped dead before him.
Most of the scholars of biography and history and the people of exegesis hold that the event of the Elephant took place in the year in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was born, so as to be a prominent landmark in history and an enduring honour for the Prophet ﷺ.

safi-cedvel:2-5.t:
* I'rab:
(the hamza) is like the first. (في تضليل) is attached to an omitted element, a second direct object. (عليهم) is attached to (أرسل), (أبابيل) is a naʿt of (طيرا), accusative, and it is denied tanwīn because of the form of the "ultimate plural" (muntahā al-jumūʿ). (بحجارة) is attached to (ترميهم), (من سجّيل) is attached to an adjective of (حجارة), (كعصف) is attached to an omitted element, a second direct object..
Clause: «لم يجعل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «أرسل ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يجعل.
And the clause: «ترميهم ... » is in the position of accusative, a second naʿt of (طيرا).
And the clause: «جعلهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أرسل.

* Morphology:
(2) تضليل: the regular maṣdar of the quadriliteral ضلّل; its wazn is تفعيل.
(3) أبابيل: a collective noun (ism jamʿ) with no singular from its own wording; it was said that its singular is إبّول on the wazn of سنّور, or أبّول on the wazn of عصفور, or إبّيل on the wazn of سكّين, or إبّال on the wazn of مفتاح.
(5) عصف: a name for the leaves of crops or their chaff, on the wazn of the maṣdar فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(5) مأكول: a passive participle from the triliteral أكل; its wazn is مفعول.

* Rhetoric:
Simile: in His saying, the Exalted: «فَجَعَلَهُمْ كَعَصْفٍ مَأْكُولٍ».
Here He likened them to eaten chaff – which is the straw of wheat – for its being emptied of its grain and blown about; or He likened the severing of their limbs to the scattering of the parts of dung that animals have eaten and excreted. It is thus a likening of a sensory thing to a sensory thing.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
[Translator's note: this entry begins mid-sentence in the source, evidently the end of the discussion of the word «الفيل» (the elephant); translated as it stands.]
It is pluralised as «fuyūl» and «fiyala» in the plural of abundance, and «afyāl» in the plural of paucity.
His saying: {أَلَمْ تَرَ}: this is the reading of the majority, I mean with fatḥa on the rāʾ, the alif being dropped because of the jussive. Al-Sulamī read «تَرْ» with sukūn on the rāʾ, as if he did not count the dropping of the alif, as in their saying «lam ubalhu». He also read «تَرْءَ» with sukūn on the rāʾ and a hamza with fatḥa, which is the original form. «كيف» suspends (muʿalliqa) the seeing, and it is accusative by a verb after it.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {أَبَابِيلَ}: an adjective (naʿt) of «طير», because that is a collective noun (ism jamʿ). Of «abābīl» it was said that it has no singular, like «asāṭīr» and «ʿabādīd»; it was also said that its singular is «ibbawl», like «ʿijjawl»; or «ibbāl»; or «ibbīl», like «sikkīn». Al-Raqāshī related that he heard «ibbāla» with shadda, and al-Farrāʾ related «ibāla» without shadda. Al-abābīl means groups, one after another. The poet said:
4644 - طريقٌ وَجبَّارٌ رِواءٌ أصولُهُ ... عليه أبابيلٌ من الطيرِ تَنْعَبُ
(A path, and a tall date-palm with well-watered roots; on it, flocks of birds croak.)
It is sometimes used figuratively for other than birds, as in his saying:
4645 - كادَتْ تُهَدُّ مِنَ الأصوات راحلتي ... إذ سالَتِ الأرضُ بالجُرْدِ الأبابيلِ
(My mount nearly collapsed at the sounds, when the ground flowed with sleek-coated troops of horses.)

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {تَرْمِيهِم}: an attribute of «طير». The majority read «تَرْميهم» with the feminine. Abū Ḥanīfa, Ibn Yaʿmar, ʿĪsā and Ṭalḥa read it with yāʾ (the masculine). Both are clear, because a collective noun can be treated as masculine or feminine. An example of the feminine is the saying:
4646 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كالطَّيْرِ تَنْجو مِنْ الشُّؤْبوب ذي البَرَدِ
(. . . like birds escaping from the downpour with hail.)
It was also said that the pronoun refers to «ربُّك», that is, "your Lord throws them". «مِنْ سِجِّيل» is an attribute of «حِجارة». «وكعَصْفٍ» is the second object of "making" (jaʿl) in the sense of "turning into". In it there is a fine intensification (mubālagha): it was not enough for Him to make them the most worthless thing in the crop, which is what yields no benefit, until He made them dung.

ukberi-tibyan:3-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَرْسَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ طَيْرًا أَبَابِيلَ (٣) تَرْمِيهِمْ بِحِجَارَةٍ مِنْ سِجِّيلٍ (٤) فَجَعَلَهُمْ كَعَصْفٍ مَأْكُولٍ (٥)).
The words of the Exalted (أَبَابِيلَ): it is said that it is a plural with no singular from its own root letters. It is also said that its singular is «إِبَّوْل», like «عِجَّوْل»; it is also said that its singular is «إِبِّيل»; and it is also said «إِبَّال». (تَرْمِيهِمْ) is a naʿt (adjective) of «طَيْر». The kāf is the second object. And Allah knows best. [Translator's note: the printed text vocalizes the second singular as «إِبَّيْل».]

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Fīl
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأصْحابِ الفِيلِ﴾ ("have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the people of the elephant?"): ”كَيْفَ“ is in the position of the accusative (fī mawḍiʿ naṣb) by ”فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ“, not by His saying ”ألَمْ تَرَ“, because ”كَيْفَ“ is one of the interrogative particles [and so is not governed by what precedes it]. The meaning of ”ألَمْ تَرَ“ is ”ألَمْ تَعْلَمْ؟“ ("have you not known?"). So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed His Messenger of narratives from the past and of what in them points to Allah's oneness and to His exalting the matter of His Kaʿba.
Part of the story of the people of the elephant is that a group of Arabs were in the land of the Negus, near a house that was a place of prayer for the Christians and the companions of the Negus. They kindled a fire which they used for some of their needs, then departed without putting it out; the wind carried it until it burned the house that was their place of prayer and a place of resort for the Negus and his companions. So he [Translator's note: the source does not name him; the account refers to the Abyssinian ruler's army, led in the usual narrative by Abraha] set out for Mecca, intending to burn the Sacred House and to make the people of Mecca lawful prey. When they drew near the Sanctuary (ḥaram), their mounts would not carry them toward the House, but when they turned them back they went. So Allah admonished them with the most eloquent of admonitions, yet they persisted in heading for the House and in [intending] to burn it. So Allah sent against them birds in flocks (abābīl), and made their plot go astray, that is, into loss and destruction. With each bird were three stones: a stone in its beak and two stones in its feet. A stone of them would fall on a man's head and come out of his rear; on each stone was the name of the man on whom it fell. So Allah, exalted be His praise, said: ﴿وَأرْسَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ طَيْرًا أبابِيلَ﴾ [al-Fīl: 3] ("and He sent against them birds in flocks"): groups from here and groups from there; and the meaning is: Allah sent against them these birds with these stones from every side.
And the meaning of ﴿تَرْمِيهِمْ بِحِجارَةٍ مِن سِجِّيلٍ﴾ [al-Fīl: 4] ("pelting them with stones of sijjīl"): Allah described, in the case of everyone He punished with stones, that they were ”مِن سِجِّيلٍ“; He said about the people of Lot: ﴿وَأمْطَرْنا عَلَيْها حِجارَةً مِن سِجِّيلٍ مَنضُودٍ﴾ [Hūd: 82] ("and We rained upon it stones of sijjīl, layered"). So the meaning is: "and He sent against them what pelted them with stones of sijjīl", that is, of His severe punishment. When the Arabs describe something hateful with sijjīl, they seem to mean severity by it, and nothing but what is hateful is described with it. The poet said:
وَرَجْلَةً يَضْرِبُونَ البَيْضَ ضاحِيَةً ∗∗∗ ضَرْبًا تَواصَتْ بِهِ الأبْطالُ سِجِّيلا
(And foot-soldiers striking the helmets in broad daylight, with a blow that heroes have commended to one another, severe [sijjīl].)
That is: a severe blow. As for ﴿أبابِيلَ﴾ [al-Fīl: 3], Abū ʿUbayda said: it has no singular. Others said: ”إبّالَةٌ“ and ”أبابِيلُ“; ”إبّالَةٌ“ being as if it were a group. Some said: its singular is ”إبُولٌ“ and [the plural] ”أبابِيلُ“, like ”عُجُولٌ“ and ”عَجاجِيلُ“.

zajjaj:5-5.t: ﴿فَجَعَلَهم كَعَصْفٍ مَأْكُولٍ﴾ ("and He made them like eaten-up straw"): that is, He made them like the leaves of crops that have dried and been eaten, that is, into which the eating blight (al-ukāl) has fallen. And it has come in the exegesis that Allah the Exalted sent a flood against them which carried them to the sea.
